description: From March 18 to May 28, 1871, Paris governed itself for **72 days**. The experience ends in Bloody Week, a repression that leaves a lasting mark on French memory.

hero.hook: 72 days where Paris governs itself… before being crushed in blood.

blocks.text: From **March 18** to **May 28, 1871**, Paris is experiencing a rare experience: the **Municipality**. For **72 days**, the capital governs itself. She refuses to obey the government installed in **Versailles** and attempts a more social democracy.
This uprising was born from a national defeat, a hungry siege and a divide between a radical Paris and a more conservative province. It ends with **Bloody Week**.

Everything starts from the [[The Franco-Prussian War (1870-1871)]] (**1870-1871**). The French emperor **Napoleon III** is captured at **Sedan**. Paris then endured a four-month siege. We eat horses, zoo animals, then rats. The capitulation seems humiliating.

blocks.caption: Parisian barricades during the Commune of 1871.

blocks.text: At Christmas **1870**, certain luxury restaurants served elephant parfait or kangaroo stew, from the Jardin des Plantes menagerie.

In February, led a mainly monarchist Assembly, withdrawn to Versailles. On **March 18**, he wanted to seize the cannons of the [[Adolphe Thiers]], a militia of armed Parisians, stored in **Montmartre**. The crowd fraternizes with the soldiers. Thiers evacuates Paris. A Central Committee takes control of the city. [[National Guard]]

sections.title: After the defeat and the siege

blocks.text: On **March 28**, the Commune was proclaimed. Workers, craftsmen, journalists, close to the [[Labor International]] (a network of unions and workers' parties): the council legislates urgently. Remission of rents. Abolition of night work for bakers. Abandoned workshops handed over to cooperatives.

blocks.caption: The Town Hall, the political heart of the Commune.

blocks.text: She also proclaimed the separation of Church and State, secular and free schools, and had the **Vendôme column**, symbol of the Empire, torn down. , teacher and activist, embodies the central role of women in clubs and on the barricades. [[Louise Michel]]

On **May 21**, the troops of Versailles entered Paris. It's **Bloody Week**. Neighborhood by neighborhood, barricade by barricade, the repression is fierce. Hostages are shot. The Tuileries and the Hôtel de Ville burn.

blocks.caption: Bloody Week: Paris taken back street by street.

blocks.text: During the Commune, the red flag became the official emblem of Paris, replacing the tricolor deemed too linked to the powers which had capitulated.

The [[Fédérés]], the name given to the supporters of the Commune, retreated to the **Père-Lachaise** cemetery. **147** last fighters were shot there at the **Wall of the Federates**. Results: between **10, 000 and 30, 000** deaths in one week, then deportations to New Caledonia.

For the philosopher **Karl Marx** and the International, the Commune was the first experience of workers' power. However, its repression consolidates the “order” **Third Republic**. Communard ideas (secularism, social rights) would later return to republican law.

events.detail: Thiers fails to seize the cannons; Paris is rocking.
events.title: Montmartre

blocks.text: In **72 days**, the Paris Commune attempted radical social democracy, before being destroyed during Bloody Week, at the cost of tens of thousands of deaths.
